original_title: Genmab's Rina-S shows durable responses in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer in Phase 2 - Dealroom
title: Genmab's Rina-S holds up against platinum-resistant ovarian cancer in Phase 2
blurb: Durable responses reported in a Phase 2 trial, and platinum resistance is exactly the setting where ovarian cancer therapies usually stop working. Promising, but it's still Phase 2.

original_title: Chemically Induced Proximity for Targeted Protein O- GlcNAcylation
title: Pointing OGT and OGA at one protein instead of all of them at once
blurb: A conspectus on using chemically induced proximity to recruit O-GlcNAc transferase or OGlcNAcase to a single chosen substrate, sidestepping what happens when you just inhibit either enzyme and get proteome-wide effects you can't pin on any one protein. The point is finally being able to ask what one O-GlcNAcylation event does, instead of guessing from a blunt knockdown.

original_title: Ligachem, Abion co-develop iADC and secure rights to five cancer targets - CHOSUNBIZ - Chosunbiz
title: Ligachem and Abion team up on iADCs, lock down five cancer targets
blurb: A co-development deal pairing Ligachem's ADC work with Abion's iADC platform, with rights secured across five cancer targets. Business news, no data attached.

original_title: Disulphide maintenance systems and proteostasis
title: Who keeps your disulfide bonds in line depends on which compartment you're in
blurb: A review tracing how cells manage disulfide bonds compartment by compartment: thioredoxin and glutaredoxin pulling them apart where reduction is wanted, PDI, Mia40, and Dsb systems building them properly where structure needs them. Same bond, same chemistry, but whether it helps or wrecks folding comes down entirely to where it forms.
venue: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B Biological Sciences

original_title: Chemically modified gelatin derivatives: synthetic strategies, physicochemical properties, biodegradation, drug delivery and biomedical applications
title: Gelatin gets the chemistry-set treatment for drug delivery duty
blurb: A review rounding up how gelatin, an old pharmaceutical excipient, gets chemically modified, amination and thiolation among others, into hydrogels, nanoparticles, and microspheres for drug delivery. An ancient ingredient with a modern makeover, and since it's a survey there's no new data of its own.

original_title: Supramolecular Hemoglobin−PEG Polymerization Equilibria as the Structural Basis for Providing Size-Controlled Polymer Particles
title: Hemoglobin as its own polymer building block
blurb: Hb already dissociates into alpha-beta dimers on its own, so they bridged the beta subunits of two Hb tetramers with four-armed PEG (10 or 40 kDa) to make bicyclic monomers. Crank the concentration and these undergo ring-opening polymerization, stepping predictably from discrete monomers to particles to a fully percolated gel. Size control for free, just by tuning concentration.

original_title: Bifunctional ligand-enabled gold-catalyzed cycloisomerization of 2'-ethynylbiaryl-2-yl carbonyl compounds
title: A ligand that relays its own proton so gold vinylidenes stop needing a stoichiometric crutch
blurb: Gold(I) vinylidenes are useful but fleeting, and until now making them meant halide/silyl migration tricks or dual-gold catalysis on diynes. This bifunctional biaryl phosphine carries a remote amide that grabs the proton itself, forming the gold acetylide without an external base, turning what used to be a Fürstner stoichiometric method into a catalytic one.

original_title: Dose-activity relationship in [(131)I]NaI therapy for differentiated thyroid carcinoma.
title: Dialing in the I-131 dose for thyroid cancer
blurb: Looks at how activity administered in I-131 NaI therapy actually tracks with dose delivered in differentiated thyroid carcinoma. No numbers to go on here, just the relationship itself.

original_title: Deciphering the Origin of Divergent Cycloisomerization Pathways in Gold(I)‐ and Silver(I)‐Catalyzed Reactions of 1,9‐Dien‐4‐yne Ester
title: Gold and silver cycloize the same yne ester into different products, DFT explains why
blurb: Gold(I) and silver(I) catalyze cycloisomerization of the same 1,9-dien-4-yne ester but land on different products. A full DFT workup traces the split to how the two metals shuffle between sigma- and pi-coordinated intermediates along the pathway, not to anything obviously different in the substrate.

original_title: Ligand design broadens NiI-catalysed C(sp2)–heteroatom couplings of aryl bromides at low catalyst loadings
title: Nickel catalysis gets a ligand that can finally handle more aryl bromides
blurb: Ni(I)/Ni(III) coupling skips the ligand-balancing act Pd needs because the bond-forming step is already favorable, but it's been held back by weak oxidative addition, which meant narrow aryl halide scope and high catalyst loadings. New ligand design fixes the oxidative addition bottleneck, broadening C(sp2)-heteroatom coupling to more aryl bromides at low loadings.

original_title: Branched-Selective, Catalytic Allene Hydrocarbonation Enabled by Ir(I)/dFppe complexes
title: Getting C-H addition across allenes to go branched on purpose
blurb: A Synpacts rundown of their own Ir(I)/dFppe system, a perfluorinated bisphosphine that steers allylic C-H addition across allenes toward the branched product instead of linear, working across pyrrole carboxamides, furans and acrylamides. It's a summary of the method, not new data.

original_title: Bispecific antibodies that engage pIgR enrich in mucosa in cynomolgus monkeys
title: Using pIgR as a backdoor into mucosal tissue
blurb: Bispecific antibodies built to engage pIgR, the receptor that normally ferries IgA across epithelium, show mucosal enrichment in cynomolgus monkeys. Monkey data only, but it's a plausible route to getting antibodies where mucosal disease actually lives.

original_title: Synthesis, characterization, and DFT study of a Pd(II) Schiff base complex: Exploration of its catalytic efficacy in the Suzuki cross-coupling reaction and its antibacterial activity
title: Yet another Schiff base Pd complex doing Suzuki coupling and killing bacteria
blurb: A naphthaldehyde/diamine Schiff base ligand complexed with Pd(II), run through the standard characterization gauntlet (NMR, mass spec, UV-vis, FTIR, DFT), then tested for both Suzuki coupling activity and antibacterial action. The two-jobs-one-complex format is common in this corner of the literature, so the real question is whether the catalytic numbers beat the simpler Pd systems already out there.

original_title: A Sterically Encumbered Triarylborane Enabling CO2 Reduction to Formate by Electrons and Protons
title: A boron radical anion that survives half a second, long enough to turn CO2 into formate
blurb: Borohydrides are the usual hydride source but making them normally needs harsh reducing metal hydrides. This sterically packed thioether-triarylborane is air- and moisture-stable, takes a one-electron reduction at -2.62 V with a radical anion lasting about 0.5 s in THF, enough time for bimolecular chemistry to happen, and pushing it to two-electron reduction plus protonation with KC8/[DBUH]+ gets you CO2 reduced to formate.

original_title: From bench to bedside: translating novel-target ADCs against treatment-resistant tumors
title: An ADC founder on what bench-to-bedside actually involves
blurb: An interview with Ona Therapeutics' co-founder and CEO on moving first-in-class ADCs against resistant tumors into the clinic, covering target validation, resistance biology, and linker-payload choices. It's a Q&A from someone whose job is to sell the pipeline, so take the framing accordingly.

original_title: Sulfolenocorrole as a Chameleon-Like Tecton Enabling the Construction of Multiring Fused Corroles
title: Fusing corroles tames their own non-innocence
blurb: Diels-Alder chemistry on sulfolenocorrole opens up a meso,beta fusion mode on top of the usual beta,beta one, stitching multiple rings into one conjugated system (CuF3x) with absorption stretching out to 1280 nm. The real payoff is electronic, not just structural: all that fusion quiets the corrole ligand's usual non-innocent behavior, and calculations plus NMR peg CuF3x as weakly antiaromatic and the free-base version as nonaromatic.

original_title: Structural and Combinatorial Design Principles of Emerging Drug Carriers
title: A tour of what drug carriers are built from these days
blurb: A review of the drug-carrier toolbox, lipids, synthetic polymers, peptides, polysaccharides, and how their tunability and modularity get leveraged for targeted delivery. A map of the field rather than a new result.

original_title: Silver‐ or Photopromoted Ring‐Opening Trifluoromethylselenolation of Epoxides With [Me 4 N][SeCF 3 ]
title: Same epoxide, two different SeCF3 products depending on whether you reach for silver or a lamp
blurb: Epoxides plus [Me4N][SeCF3] and a carboxylic acid under AgClO4 give trifluoromethylselenyl esters up to 92% yield. Swap in purple LEDs and water instead of silver and you get hydroxytrifluoromethylselenolated products up to 86%. One reagent, one substrate class, two divergent difunctionalizations just by picking which activation mode you use.

original_title: Visible‐Light‐Driven Photoredox [2 + 1] Cycloaddition of Sulfoxonium Ylides With Alkenes
title: Cyclopropanes from sulfoxonium ylides, no metal in sight
blurb: Visible light kicks a carbon radical off a sulfoxoxium ylide via single-electron oxidation, and an SN2 step onto the alkene closes the cyclopropane ring, no metal catalyst or additives needed. Worth noting since most cyclopropanation routes are still leaning on precious metals and harsher conditions to make a motif that's everywhere in drugs and natural products.

original_title: Visible‐Light‐Mediated Photoredox 1,2‐Aryl Migration of Allylic Alcohols With Sulfoxonium Ylides for the Synthesis of 1,5‐Dicarbonyl Scaffolds
title: Allylic alcohols and sulfoxonium ylides, rerouted into 1,5-dicarbonyls
blurb: A metal-free photoredox 1,2-aryl migration turns allylic alcohols and sulfoxonium ylides into 1,5-dicarbonyl compounds, which then convert into pyridines in a one-pot two-step sequence. Broad functional-group tolerance claimed, and it's a step- and atom-economical way to reach two useful scaffolds from one reaction.

original_title: Metal‐Templated Dynamic Reorganization of Macrocyclic Gold Complexes Toward an N ‐Doped Cycloparaphenylene Catenane
title: Gold and copper trade dynamic bonds to lock a cycloparaphenylene into a catenane
blurb: Strained, fully conjugated cycloparaphenylene rings resist being forced into interlocked catenanes because you'd need to build the topology and reorganize a rigid backbone at the same time. Here reversible Au(I)-C exchange and exchangeable Cu(I)-N coordination run as two orthogonal dynamic processes that get coupled together to template an N-doped CPP catenane. Getting two self-assembly handles to cooperate instead of fight is the actual trick.

original_title: Influence of Ligand Denticity and Nuclearity on the Catalytic Activity and Product Selectivity in Oxygen Reduction Reaction Catalyzed by Copper(II) Complexes
title: Denticity alone swings a copper ORR catalyst's activity 17-fold
blurb: Two Cu(II) complexes built on otherwise similar aminopyridyl ligands, one pentadentate, one tetradentate, differ in oxygen reduction activity by about 17x. Kinetics point to a proton-coupled electron transfer step as the reason the extra donor arm matters.

original_title: An Energetic-Control Framework for Electrospray Ionization Using Thermometer Ions
title: A way to actually know how hot your ESI source is running
blurb: ESI-MS users tweak source settings constantly, deliberately or just during method tuning, without knowing the energetic consequences, so differences between experiments can come from ion activation rather than real solution or droplet chemistry. This framework uses thermometer ions to put a number on that, so you can tell whether a reactive intermediate actually changed or your source just got more aggressive.
venue: Journal of the American Society for Mass Spectrometry

original_title: Single-molecule chromatin tracing reveals a diversity of megabase heterochromatin domains.
title: Megabase heterochromatin isn't one uniform blob
blurb: Single-molecule chromatin tracing turns up a real diversity of megabase-scale heterochromatin domain types rather than a single uniform structure.

original_title: Molecular Engineering at Electrode Interface Enables Efficient Catalytic Nitrogen Reduction
title: Pinning a molecular Mo catalyst to the electrode instead of letting it drift
blurb: Homogeneous N2-fixation catalysts mostly waste themselves sitting in bulk solution, so this group anchored a molecular Mo complex (PyMoBr3PNP) onto graphdiyne via pi-pi stacking and wired it straight onto a carbon-paper electrode. The resulting PyMoBr3PNP/GDY/CP assembly converts N2 to ammonia using a pyridinium triflate proton source. The fix is catalyst utilization, not a new mechanism, but that's the part that's actually been limiting these systems.

original_title: Amide‐Enabled Reversal of Regioselectivity in Carbonyl‐Substituted Allenes
title: An amide NH flips where the nucleophile lands on allenes
blurb: Carbonyl-conjugated allenes normally push nucleophilic addition to the beta position, but a secondary amide built into the allene flips that to alpha-selective acyloxylation with carboxylic acids under rhodium catalysis, no oxidant or bolted-on directing group needed. Swap that amide for a ketone, ester, or N-methyl amide and the effect disappears, so it's specifically the NH doing the steering.

original_title: Mitochondria-Targeted Prodrug Nanoassemblies Elicit Antitumor Immunity via Mitophagy-Boosted Ferroptosis in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer
title: A mitochondria-seeking prodrug that triggers ferroptosis through mitophagy
blurb: Sulfasalazine gets hitched to triphenylphosphonium through a disulfide linker and self-assembles into carrier-free nanoparticles that home to mitochondria, where the chemistry releases the drug and boosts mitophagy to drive ferroptosis in triple-negative breast cancer. The pitch is that this also stirs up antitumor immunity rather than just killing cells, in a cancer whose iron-starved, GPX4-happy biology usually blunts ferroptosis.

original_title: Reconstruction robustness of liver-referenced adaptive thresholding for (68)Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT volumetry: a comparative analysis of systematic bias and individual-patient variability.
title: How much does your PET reconstruction change the PSMA tumor volume
blurb: A comparison of how reconstruction settings shift liver-referenced adaptive thresholding for Ga-68 PSMA-11 PET/CT, splitting out systematic bias from the variability you'd see from patient to patient. Worth knowing if you're leaning on these volumes for dosimetry or tracking response.

original_title: Universal charge-tag labelling of undetectable polymers for mass spectrometric characterization.
title: A charge tag for polymers mass spec can't normally see
blurb: A labelling method that bolts a charge tag onto polymers that otherwise ionize too poorly to show up on mass spec, pitched as a general fix rather than a one-off workaround.

original_title: Phenoxazinone synthase functional mimic activity of mixed-ligand copper(II) complexes of L-proline and diimine ligands conjugated with chitosan
title: Chitosan-bound copper complexes that moonlight as an enzyme
blurb: Chitosan-conjugated proline ligands paired with bipyridine or phenanthroline and copper(II) give two mixed-ligand complexes that mimic phenoxazinone synthase, the bacterial copper enzyme behind that oxidation chemistry. A green-catalysis spin on enzyme mimicry, with the ligand parked on a polymer instead of floating free.

original_title: AstraZeneca, Daiichi Sankyo & Summit team up to test cancer drug combination - Indian Pharma Post
title: AstraZeneca, Daiichi Sankyo and Summit pair up on a cancer combo
blurb: The three are teaming up to test a cancer drug combination. No word yet on which drugs or what indication.

original_title: Ag─S Sites Steer Furfural Electroreduction to Furfuryl Alcohol
title: A little sulfide turns silver into the right catalyst for furfural
blurb: Trace sulfide in the electrolyte builds Ag-S sites on silver electrodes on the fly, and that's what pushes furfural electroreduction toward furfuryl alcohol instead of the C-C coupled dimers that usually compete with hydrogenation. The catalyst is forming itself mid-reaction rather than being made in advance.

original_title: Network Constraint Density and Structure–Property Relationships in Branched Sulfonated Poly( para -phenylene) Membranes for Water Electrolysis
title: Branching sulfonated poly(p-phenylene) to loosen up proton transport
blurb: SPP membranes owe their stability to a rigid, ether-free backbone, but that rigidity packs the chains too tightly for protons to move through easily. Working in 0-5 mol% of a trifunctional branching unit during synthesis and tracking the resulting network constraint density against swelling, conductivity, and oxidative stability, to see what loosening the packing costs the stability SPP is prized for in the first place.

original_title: Design, Synthesis, and Biological Evaluation of Novel Tetrazole-Containing Tetrahydroisoquinoline Derivatives as Putative CYP51 Inhibitors against Candida Species
title: Patching up a fast-clearing CYP51 inhibitor against Candida
blurb: Lead compound A33 was potent but gone in under 3 minutes (t1/2 = 2.89 min), so bioisostere swaps and scaffold tweaks on a tetrazole-tetrahydroisoquinoline series went after both that and the CYP inhibition liability that dogs azole-type antifungals. The result, LH23, keeps the anti-Candida activity with better metabolic stability and less CYP baggage.

original_title: Proximity‐Induced Disulfide Rebridging Enables Modular Construction of Stable Antibody–Drug Conjugates
title: A rebridging reagent that stops making you choose between fast and stable
blurb: Disulfide rebridging for ADCs has usually meant picking a lane: quick conjugation that falls apart, or a stable linkage that reacts too slowly to be practical. This heterotrifunctional reagent, a 5-fluoro-4-(phenylsulfonyl)pyridine derivative, splits the kinetics so the bridging and the locking-in happen on different timescales, letting them build a range of stable ADC architectures off one scaffold.

original_title: SMP-656: A self-catalyzed ring-opening hydrolysis linker-based ADC with enhanced stability and antitumor efficacy
title: A linker that opens itself
blurb: SMP-656 pairs ADC payloads to a self-catalyzed ring-opening hydrolysis linker, with the med-chem write-up reporting better stability and antitumor efficacy than whatever it's being compared against.

original_title: Click-to-Release Reactivity of Quaternary Anilinium Tetrazines Enables Cascade Assembly of Multifunctional Biomolecular Scaffolds.
title: A tetrazine release reaction that stops wasting itself on dead ends
blurb: Click-to-release chemistry with tetrazine/TCO pairs usually bleeds efficiency into dead-end intermediates along the way. Swapping the standard carbamate linker for a quaternary anilinium leaving group redirects that mess into a working cascade, enough to assemble multifunctional biomolecular scaffolds instead of just stalling out mid-reaction.

original_title: Click‐to‐Release Reactivity of Quaternary Anilinium Tetrazines Enables Cascade Assembly of Multifunctional Biomolecular Scaffolds
title: Rewiring tetrazine click-to-release through an anilinium leaving group
blurb: Tetrazine/TCO click-to-release is mechanistically messy, prone to dead-end intermediates that eat into how much cargo actually gets released. Here the usual carbamate linkage is swapped for a quaternary anilinium leaving group, and that complexity gets turned into a cascade that assembles multifunctional scaffolds step by step rather than just releasing once.

original_title: Preliminary Evaluation of Synthetic Amanitin Analogs as Novel Payloads for Potent Antibody−Drug Conjugates
title: Lab-made death cap toxins, benchmarked against the real thing
blurb: Alpha-amanitin, the toxin that makes death cap mushrooms lethal, is being repurposed as an ADC payload. Three synthetic amatoxin analogs already flagged as more cytotoxic than the natural toxin get hooked to trastuzumab via a glutaric linker for a direct head-to-head against alpha-amanitin itself. Preliminary, but a real comparison rather than just another cytotoxicity screen.

original_title: Semisynthesis of Multiphosphorylated and Acetylated Histone Methyltransferase Dot1L Reveals Synergistic Inhibition of Nucleosomal H3K79 Methylation
title: Dot1L has its own off-switch, built from phosphorylation and acetylation
blurb: Dot1L's regulation via ubiquitin marks on its histone substrates is well charted, but the modifications sitting on Dot1L's own lysine-rich region were a blank spot. Semisynthesis installs combinations of phosphorylation and acetylation there and finds they don't just add up, they synergize to shut down nucleosomal H3K79 methylation, the mark that goes haywire in leukemia.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Advances in radiolabeled antibody technology: optimization strategies for precision medicine.
title: A rundown of where radiolabeled antibodies stand
blurb: A review of optimization strategies for radiolabeled antibody technology aimed at precision medicine, summarizing the field rather than reporting new data.

original_title: HER2-Targeted Antibody-Drug Conjugates in Advanced HER2-Low Breast Cancer: Mechanisms, Clinical Efficacy, and Resistance Strategies.
title: HER2-low breast cancer's ADC playbook, reviewed
blurb: A review of HER2-targeted ADCs in advanced HER2-low breast cancer, walking through the mechanisms, the clinical efficacy data, and how resistance shows up and gets countered. A survey, not new results.

original_title: Impact of Time and Temperature on Glycation, Oxidation, and Functional Stability of Trastuzumab Deruxtecan (ENHERTU®) in Dextrose Infusion Bags
title: How long you can actually leave Enherту sitting in the bag
blurb: Trastuzumab deruxtecan's label gives diluted infusion bags a tight leash, 24 hours refrigerated or 4 hours at room temp, which means tossed doses whenever a clinic's timing slips. This one tracks glycation, oxidation, and functional stability across time and temperature to see whether that window is actually as conservative as it looks.

original_title: Complex Fragment Coupling via O -Mesyl Hydroxylamines: Direct Conversion of Primary Amines to Electrophilic Aminating Agents
title: Turning an amine into its own electrophile, in one step
blurb: Electrophilic amination usually tops out at simple nitrogen groups because there's no easy way to make complex NH-alkyl electrophiles. Direct single-step oxidation converts primary amines straight into N-alkyl-O-mesyl hydroxylamines, so whatever complex amine fragment you've already got becomes the aminating agent for the next coupling.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Aromaticity Engineering of Hybrid Cyanine Dyes for Metabolic Labeling and Bioorthogonal NIR‐II Imaging of Gut Microbiota
title: A cyanine dye redesign that lights up gut bacteria in NIR-II
blurb: Stripped the heteroatoms out of the usual xanthene scaffold and fused in a flatter, more conjugated aminofluorene instead, which boosts aromaticity enough to track bacteria deep in living tissue by NIR-II imaging. The pitch is diabetic infection risk, where immune dysfunction and microcirculation damage let gut bacteria roam, so the point is watching them migrate and colonize in real time.

original_title: Redox-Controlled Site-Specific O-Sulfation Facilitated Diversity-Oriented Chemoenzymatic Synthesis of Chondroitin Sulfates A/C/E and Chimeric Chondroitin Sulfates
title: Programming chondroitin sulfate's sulfation pattern instead of hoping the enzyme cooperates
blurb: Sulfotransferases are sloppy about where they put sulfate groups, so this swaps in a redox-controlled strategy to install CS-A, CS-C, or CS-E sequences at chosen positions along the chondroitin backbone. Netted 28 distinct oligosaccharides, including chimeras mixing sulfation types on one chain, which is the structural control CS biology has been missing.

original_title: Bridging the Gap between Discovery and Clinical Reality in Radiopharmaceuticals: A Translational Science Perspective on Safety, Efficacy, and Manufacturability
title: Why radioligand therapy still has only two FDA approvals after hundreds of trials
blurb: A translational postmortem arguing RPTs keep getting designed like ordinary targeted drugs when they're not. Radionuclide physics, carrier pharmacokinetics, tumor biology, and manufacturing all pull against each other, and that mismatch is apparently why Lutathera and Pluvicto are still the only current-generation approvals a decade into the trial boom.

original_title: Plug-and-display labeling system for modular subunit vaccine development
title: Grading the anchor chemistries behind plug-and-display vaccines
blurb: A review of the conjugation tech that lets you snap antigen and adjuvant modules onto a universal nanoscaffold. The bar for clinical use is bioorthogonal, fast, quantitative, and nontoxic all at once, and apparently nobody's nailed all four together, which is why these modular platforms keep getting proposed more than deployed.

original_title: A Radical Addition–Diradical Coupling Switch Unifies Cytochrome P450-Catalyzed Diketopiperazine Dimerization
title: One P450 switch explains how dimeric diketopiperazines get their weird link
blurb: Most P450-catalyzed DKP dimerization follows a known radical addition path, but the oddball C3-N1' linkage didn't fit that story. Structure-guided protein engineering plus crystallography finds the enzyme flips to a diradical coupling mode instead, so one switchable mechanism covers both cases rather than two separate explanations.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Mechanistic Analysis of Albumin–Ruthenium Conjugates Reveals Redox‐Sensitive Catalytic Persistence for Extracellular Prodrug Uncaging
title: An albumin-ruthenium catalyst built to work outside the cell
blurb: Most prodrug-uncaging catalysts need to get inside cells to matter. This one stays extracellular on purpose, pairing ruthenium to albumin and leaning on SPARC to concentrate near cells, with activity that depends on the local redox environment. Still a mechanistic study of the conjugate, not a tumor result yet.

original_title: Development of a Stereoselective Route for Kilogram-Scale Synthesis of STING Agonist BMS-986301
title: Kilo-scale STING agonist synthesis cuts six chromatography steps to zero
blurb: A chiral P(V) reagent enables diastereoselective thiophosphoramidate chemistry, and the production route built on it swaps column purification for crystallization at six separate steps. Fewer steps, no hazardous reagents, an eightfold yield bump, and 90% less process mass intensity, the unglamorous process chemistry that actually decides whether a drug ships.

original_title: The radical-radical cross-coupling of alkyl carboxylic acids and organoborons
title: Carboxylic acids and boronic acids finally cross-couple without the radicals going rogue
blurb: Both are cheap feedstocks but their radicals don't recombine cleanly on their own. Alternating-polarity electrolysis times the radical generation on each side so they pair up instead of running wild, giving a general route to C(sp3)-C(sp3) bonds out of two of the most boring, abundant functional groups around.

original_title: Genmab’s latest phase 2 data spur claim ADC is ‘clearly superior’ to AbbVie’s Elahere
title: Genmab's ADC posts 9.5 months PFS and the analysts are already calling it better than Elahere
blurb: TD Cowen is out saying Genmab's antibody-drug conjugate is 'clearly superior' to AbbVie's Elahere off phase 2 numbers. It's one readout, and the house declaring a winner has a stake in you believing it, so file 'clearly superior' under sales pitch until there's an actual head-to-head.

original_title: The tRNA‐Modification Geranyl‐2‐Thiouridine Enables RNA‐Lipid Association
title: A tRNA wobble modification that makes RNA stickier to lipid
blurb: Geranyl-2-thiouridine sits at the wobble position of certain tRNAs in nature, and that geranyl tail turns out to make RNA more lipophilic. LNP formulations currently brute-force RNA-lipid binding with a lot of cationic lipid, so a modification doing some of that work chemically could mean needing less of it.

original_title: Consecutive hydrodefluorination for the regioselective synthesis of partially fluorinated arenes
title: Perfluoroarenes, defluorinated just the right amount
blurb: Hydridosilicates generated in situ from phenylsilane and cesium carbonate strip fluorines off perfluoroarenes one round at a time, all in one pot, so you can stop at di- or trifluoroarenes instead of overshooting to monofluoro. That middle ground has been the annoying part to hit selectively, so this is worth watching if the regioselectivity survives outside their reported substrates.

original_title: Radical Markovnikov Hydroboration of Unactivated Terminal Alkenes With HBaza‐Type Hydroborane via a Triple Catalysis
title: Getting Markovnikov selectivity out of a hydroboration for once
blurb: Hydroboration of terminal alkenes usually hands you the anti-Markovnikov product by default. This triple-catalysis setup with an HBaza-type hydroborane flips that for unactivated terminal alkenes, with a broad substrate scope reported, useful if you actually wanted the boron on the internal carbon.

original_title: Enantioselective Synthesis of Chiral 3-Substituted Tetrahydroquinolines via a Pd-Catalyzed C–C Cleavage/C–C Coupling Sequence
title: Cracking a C-C bond open to build chiral tetrahydroquinolines
blurb: Pd(OAc)2 with Josiphos L7 cleaves a cyclobutanol tethered to a bromoaniline and recombines the pieces into 3-substituted tetrahydroquinolines carrying a C3-ketone, good yields and enantioselectivities. Only the cis-substrates reacted, which says the mechanism is picky about geometry, not just electronics.

original_title: Role of the Benzyl Substituent in Binding of f‐Elements by Diglycolamides: A Combined Solvent Extraction, Spectroscopic, and X‐Ray Diffraction Study
title: Tacking benzyl groups onto diglycolamides to pull actinides away from uranium
blurb: Two new benzyl-substituted diglycolamides, checked by solvent extraction, spectroscopy, and X-ray structures, show the amide substituents control both selectivity and the makeup of the extracted complex. They found conditions to purify An(III) and An(IV) away from uranium and most fission products, which is the actual payoff: a nuclear separations problem, not a catalysis one.

original_title: Inhibition of pancreatic cancer growth by an siRNA targeting SNORA22 and a folic acid-conjugated cationic oligopeptide
title: Smuggling an siRNA into pancreatic tumors on a folate leash
blurb: An siRNA against SNORA22, a small nucleolar RNA pushing pancreatic cancer growth, gets delivered by a new regioisomer of a folic-acid-conjugated cationic octapeptide built to survive systemic circulation long enough to reach the tumor. The target is the less obvious part here; getting anything past PDAC's barriers intact is the real engineering problem they're solving.

original_title: Structural Diversification of Fangchinoline via a CuAAC Reaction: Design, Batch and Semi‐Flow Synthesis, and Anticancer Activity Evaluation
title: Click chemistry gives fangchinoline a triazole facelift
blurb: Late-stage CuAAC chemistry bolts 1,2,3-triazoles onto fangchinoline at C7, and three of the resulting derivatives, FC01, FC03, and FC05, show strong activity against HeLa, MCF-7, and HCT-116 respectively. They also moved the synthesis into a loop flow reactor for better yields, the kind of detail that matters more to scale-up than to the anticancer story.

original_title: Tumor microenvironment-responsive injectable hydrogels for localized therapy of pancreatic cancer.
title: An injectable hydrogel that waits for the tumor before releasing anything
blurb: A hydrogel tuned to respond to the pancreatic tumor microenvironment, aimed at keeping the therapy localized rather than circulating systemically.

original_title: 99mTc radiolabeled papain nanoparticle: In silico dosimetry evaluation using Monte Carlo codes and the DM_BRA voxel phantom and OLINDA/EXM for internal dosimetry based on experimental biodistribution data
title: Running the dosimetry math on a Tc-99m papain nanoparticle before it goes near a patient
blurb: Monte Carlo dosimetry, using the DM_BRA voxel phantom and OLINDA/EXM, mapped out organ doses for a 99mTc-labeled papain nanoparticle, fed by actual experimental biodistribution data rather than assumptions. Pure in silico groundwork, the paperwork step that comes before anyone talks about using it in imaging or therapy.

original_title: Neurofibrillary tangle deposition in primary idiotypic isocortices using flortaucipir PET in histopathologically confirmed Alzheimer's disease.
title: Checking where tau tangles actually land against autopsy-confirmed Alzheimer's
blurb: Flortaucipir PET signal compared against histopathology in cases with confirmed Alzheimer's, mapping neurofibrillary tangle deposition across the isocortex. Ground-truthing the tracer against real pathology instead of just another PET comparison.

original_title: Nickel‐Catalyzed Enantioselective Addition of Aromatic, Heteroaryl, and Alkenyl Halides to Aliphatic Aldimines
title: Aryl and alkenyl halides adding to aldimines at 99% ee
blurb: Nickel complexes of rigid chiral bis(oxazoline)s add aryl, heteroaryl, and alkenyl halides to alkyl aldimines, hitting 99% ee or better across a broad scope, with low catalyst loading and runs that scale to grams. They used it to build ten medicinally relevant chiral benzylamines and azacycles, and kinetic profiling points to efficient Mn reduction, not the usual suspects, as what's actually controlling the reaction.

original_title: Synthesis of 2,3-Dihydro-4(1 H )-pyrimidinones through Copper-Catalyzed Skeletal Rearrangement of Spirocyclic Aminimides
title: Aminimides learn a trick besides losing nitrogen
blurb: Aminimides are usually just nitrene surrogates that dump N2 in Curtius-type rearrangements. Here a copper catalyst runs alkynyl hydrazides through a spirocyclic aminimide intermediate, then N-N cleavage and an intramolecular C-H insertion, landing 2,3-dihydro-4(1H)-pyrimidinones in one atom-economical step. The mechanism is inferred from control experiments rather than caught directly, but it's a new use for a reagent class that's been doing the same one trick for decades.

original_title: Modifying Catalytic Sustainability in Renaud Catalysts: Hints From Aromaticity, Conceptual DFT, and Steric Mapping
title: A computational tune-up for iron hydrogenation catalysts
blurb: Knölker-type iron complexes are the earth-abundant stand-in for Pd/Ru/Ir hydrogenation catalysts, and this study uses aromaticity analysis, conceptual DFT, and steric mapping to predict which tweaks to the cyclopentadienone ligand on Renaud catalysts actually help sustainability. All prediction so far, nobody's synthesized the winners yet.

original_title: A Visible‐Light‐Induced Strategy for C(sp 3 )─H Heteroarylation of Lactones With Quinoxalin‐2(1 H )‐Ones via Radical Processes in Water
title: Alkylating quinoxalinones with light, water, and whatever lactone's on the shelf
blurb: Visible light plus H2O2/KHSO4 pulls alkyl radicals straight out of lactones, esters, ethers, and ketones, which then graft onto quinoxalin-2(1H)-ones to build the C(sp3)-C(sp2) bond. It runs in water at room temperature, so no special radical precursors or harsh conditions needed, just a mild one-pot alkylation.

original_title: Photoexcited Palladium-Catalyzed Defluorinative 1,2-Functional-Group Migration of Allylic Alcohols
title: Breaking one C-F bond to triple-functionalize an allylic alcohol
blurb: Hitting an alkene with an aryldifluoromethyl radical usually gets you difunctionalization and nothing more. This photoexcited palladium system pushes further: selective mono-defluorination of a trifluoromethylarene, radical addition, a local 1,2-migration, and carbonyl formation, all redox-neutral and without a stoichiometric oxidant. End result is allylic alcohols turned into alpha-alkynyl, alpha-aryl, or alpha-heteroaryl ketones in one cascade.

original_title: An integrated experimental-deterministic photon transport framework for radiation dosimetry: Application to naturally occurring radioactive building materials
title: Gauging how much gamma your walls give off
blurb: An integrated experimental and deterministic photon transport model for radiation dosimetry, applied to naturally occurring radioactive building materials, the kind of dosimetry work that matters for figuring out what construction stone and concrete are actually dosing people with over time.

original_title: Modulation of the TGF‐β/Smad Signaling Pathway by a Bioactive Oxidized Polygonati Rhizoma Polysaccharide Crosslinked Chitosan Hydrogel as Therapeutic Carrier for Parkinson's Disease Treatment
title: A Parkinson's hydrogel that's doing something before the drug even goes in
blurb: An injectable, self-healing hydrogel made by crosslinking oxidized Polygonati rhizoma polysaccharide with carboxymethyl chitosan via Schiff base bonds, built as a carrier that also leans on TGF-beta/Smad signaling. With no levodopa loaded at all, it already cut ROS buildup and M1-skewed microglial activity, so the carrier itself is pulling therapeutic weight, not just ferrying the drug.

original_title: Engineering Highly Efficient Mullite SmMn 2 O 5 Catalysts for Selective Aerobic Solvent‐Free Oxidation of Toluene to Benzoic Acid
title: Nitric acid etching gives a mullite catalyst a cleaner route to benzoic acid
blurb: Toluene-to-benzoic-acid currently means homogeneous catalysts that are a pain to recover or chlorination routes that corrode equipment and leave chlorine in the product. This SmMn2O5 mullite catalyst, etched with nitric acid to open up surface area and oxygen vacancies, runs the oxidation solvent-free on plain molecular oxygen instead.

original_title: Palladium complexes of pincer-structured organosulfur ligands: coordination features, reactivity, and applications
title: A review of palladium pincers built on sulfur donors
blurb: A survey of organosulfur-ligated Pd pincer complexes, covering ligand and framework design, how they coordinate, and the structure-reactivity trends that fall out of it, with particular attention to their use in greener catalytic transformations. It's a review, so the payoff is the map it draws, not a new reaction.

original_title: Carbene transfer from thianthrenium ylides for cyclopropanation
title: Carbene transfer without the explosive precursors
blurb: Cyclopropanation has long run on diazo compounds and other intermediates chemists just accept as hazardous, since the safer alternative, sulfonium salts, has never been an efficient carbene donor. This method gets carbene transfer from thianthrenium ylides instead, opening up cyclopropanation without the usual explosion risk baked into the starting materials.

original_title: Site-Selective Radical Carbonylation of Aryl Thianthrenium Salts with Gaseous CO in Flow
title: Catching aryl radicals with gaseous CO before they can quit
blurb: Site-selective carbonylation of complex arenes is hard mainly because CO has to intercept aryl radicals that don't stick around. This photoredox method generates those radicals from aryl thianthrenium salts and catches them with gaseous CO in continuous flow, and the resulting acyl radicals then grab Michael acceptors to build 1,4-dicarbonyls. The pressurized gas-liquid flow setup is what makes the interception actually work.

original_title: Enantioselective palladium-catalyzed carbonylation of gem-dibromoalkenes to chiral benzo[7]annulenes
title: A palladium catalyst that stops at one bromide, not two
blurb: Gem-dibromoalkenes carry two reactive bromines, and getting a catalyst to touch just one enantioselectively usually loses to double functionalization and a prochiral alkene that won't pick a side. Here the dibromides are locked onto a rigid benzo[7]annulene scaffold, and the asymmetric monocarbonylation gives chiral tetrasubstituted vinyl bromides in up to 97% yield with strong enantiocontrol.

original_title: Effects of Zinc Leachate on the Structure and Activity of Semaglutide
title: Does Ozempic's own syringe leach zinc into the drug
blurb: Prefilled semaglutide pens use an elastomer needle shield that can leach zinc, and zinc leaching is already flagged as a risk for antibody drugs, causing aggregation and clogged needles. This checks whether semaglutide's own structure and activity take the same hit.

original_title: Biomolecules under Pressure: Protein Phase Transitions from Folding to Misfolding, Aggregation, and Condensation
title: Squeeze a protein instead of heating it and you see more
blurb: A review of high hydrostatic pressure as a protein probe: unlike heat or chemical denaturants, pressure leaves covalent bonds alone and only pulls apart the weaker packing forces, surfacing folding and misfolding intermediates that thermal or chemical unfolding blur past. The case rests on a decade of high-pressure NMR, fluorescence, time-resolved crystallography, and single-molecule work turning pressure into a real structural tool.

original_title: Iterative Optimization of Photoactivatable BRD4 Degraders for Aging‐Amplified Immunotherapy in Patient‐Derived Lung Cancer Organoids
title: A BRD4 degrader that only switches on where you shine light
blurb: Targeted protein degraders tend to work everywhere at once in vivo, hook effects included, with no way to aim them in space or time. This photoactivatable approach uses two-photon light to trigger degradation locally, and compound 9, reached through iterative optimization, is the first two-photon BRD4 photodegrader, tested in patient-derived lung cancer organoids under an aging-linked immunotherapy angle.

original_title: Deaminative Radical Sulfinylation Reaction
title: Turning amines into radicals to skip straight to sulfinamides
blurb: DPPH activates primary amines into radicals on the spot, which then couple with electrophilic sulfinylamine partners to give alkyl and aryl sulfinamides in moderate to good yields. The appeal is using cheap, off-the-shelf amines as the radical source instead of some more exotic precursor.

original_title: Mechanical Flipping of [1]Rotaxanes Toughens Polymer Networks
title: A one-piece rotaxane crosslinker that toughens plastic by flipping
blurb: [1]Rotaxanes, the self-interlocked single-component cousins of the better-studied [2]rotaxanes and polyrotaxanes, get used here as polymer crosslinkers. Two versions share the same entangled architecture but differ only in how hard it is to flip the ring, and that flipping barrier alone tracks with how much tougher the resulting network gets.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: A recyclable g-C3N4/Biochar@Pd hybrid nanocatalyst for high-performance Suzuki, Stille and CN coupling reactions
title: Palladium riding on biochar for cross-coupling you can reuse
blurb: A g-C3N4/biochar support loaded with Pd, built by thermal polycondensation, handles Suzuki, Stille, and C-N couplings and claims to survive being recycled. Cross-coupling catalysts built on biochar haven't really proven themselves as a general platform yet, so the recyclability claim is the part worth watching.

original_title: Sustainable and solvent-free delamination of spent LFP cathodes and their direct regeneration via stoichiometric hydrothermal re-lithiation
title: Recycling LFP batteries without melting or dissolving them
blurb: LFP cathodes carry so little raw metal value that pyrometallurgy and hydrometallurgy usually lose money recycling them. This method delaminates the spent cathode with no solvent, then relithiates it hydrothermally in a stoichiometric step, regenerating the active material directly rather than breaking it back down to metal salts first.

original_title: Targeting the capsule of Klebsiella pneumoniae with a cationic CR3-binding protein enhances phagocytosis and promotes bacterial clearance and survival in a mouse sepsis model
title: The platelet protein that flags staph for killing also flags Klebsiella
blurb: PF4 already works as an opsonin against gram-positive S. aureus by binding the CR3 phagocytic receptor. Tested here against a tougher target, encapsulated gram-negative Klebsiella pneumoniae, it still boosts phagocytosis and improves survival in a mouse sepsis model, so the pathogen-agnostic claim is holding up so far.

original_title: Emerging Nanoscale Platforms for Precision Glycan Analysis: Molecular Fingerprinting, Nanopore Sensing, and Spatial Readouts
title: Reading one sugar molecule at a time instead of averaging them
blurb: Glycans are built without a template, so every batch is a mix of close variants, and they pack more structural information per residue than DNA or protein does. This review rounds up five emerging single-molecule platforms built to handle that, including tip-enhanced Raman spectroscopy, which resolves individual glycosidic linkages by their vibrational fingerprint, alongside nanopore sensing and spatial-readout methods.

original_title: Design, Synthesis, and Anti-Inflammatory Activity Evaluation of Novel thieno[2,3- d ]Pyrimidin-4(3 H )-One-Based NLRP3 Inflammasome Inhibitors
title: A Parkinson's drug repurposed into an NLRP3 inhibitor
blurb: Istradefylline is normally an anti-Parkinsonian agent, but it also showed weak NLRP3 inflammasome inhibition on the side. They built a thieno-pyrimidinone series off that lead and landed on L22, which binds NLRP3 directly at IC50 0.16 μM, ten times tighter than the parent drug's 1.81 μM. A known drug's off-target activity doing the actual work here.

original_title: MHC-I–Driven Antitumor Immunity Counterbalances Low Absorbed Doses of Radiopharmaceutical Therapy - Journal of Nuclear Medicine
title: Why low-dose radiopharmaceuticals still kill tumors
blurb: The claim is that MHC-I-driven antitumor immunity picks up the slack when the absorbed radiation dose is too low to finish the job on its own. So at the low end of dosing, it's the immune response doing real work alongside the radiation, not just the radiation.

original_title: Investigation of Chiral Imidazoquinoline Based Heterocyclic Small Molecules on TLR7/8 Modulatory Activity
title: Same imidazoquinoline scaffold, opposite TLR7/8 effect depending on which enantiomer you pick
blurb: A library of chiral imidazoquinolines split into a potent dual TLR7/8 agonist (compound 40, EC50 78 nM at TLR7, 520 nM at TLR8) and an antagonist (compound 31, IC50 270 nM/320 nM) just by stereochemistry. Same core, opposite pharmacology, depending on which mirror image you're holding.

original_title: Discovery of Novel Pyridazine-Containing Nicotinamide Derivatives as Potent FTO Inhibitors for Acute Myeloid Leukemia
title: An FTO inhibitor that actually kills AML cells, not just binds the target
blurb: Out of 67 compounds, E6 came out on top against FTO (IC50 5.3 μM, KD 3.25 μM), with MST, CETSA, and DARTS all agreeing it hits the real target rather than something downstream. It also drove apoptosis in MOLM-13 cells and raised global m6A levels, consistent with blocking FTO's demethylase job. Still mid-micromolar, so there's distance left before this is a real AML candidate.

original_title: Unsaturated Carboxylates as Electrophilic Synthons for Transition‐Metal‐Catalyst‐Free Electroreductive Deoxygenative Coupling
title: Electroreductive coupling that skips the metal catalyst and the ester's oxygen
blurb: Unsaturated carboxylates paired with alkyl halides under a sacrificial anode, no transition metal needed, building C(sp3)-C(sp3) bonds by stripping oxygen out entirely. Aryl, alkenyl, and alkynyl carboxylates all go in, giving methylene-bridged alkylarenes plus allylic and propargylic frameworks. The mechanism is independent single-electron reduction of both electrophiles followed by radical recombination, a cleaner story than most metal-free couplings manage.

original_title: Photoinduced Electron Donor‐Acceptor Complex‐Driven Radical Cascade Strategy Toward Sulfonylated Pyrazolones
title: Pyrazolones get sulfonylated by light, no photocatalyst required
blurb: A visible-light radical cascade stitches diaryliodonium salts and DABSO onto hydrazide substrates to build arylsulfonylated pyrazolones, catalyst-free and base-free under mild conditions. The proposed trigger is the iodonium salt and DABSO interacting directly under light to kick off the sulfonyl radical, cutting the photocatalyst out of its usual job.

original_title: COPD trial wins spur broad respiratory hopes
title: Tozorakimab's COPD win puts IL-33 antibodies back on the map
blurb: AstraZeneca's anti-IL-33 antibody cut flare-ups in a COPD trial, and the read now is that IL-33-targeted antibodies could work across pulmonary disease more broadly, not just this one indication. One trial win stretched into a thesis, which is how this always goes until it doesn't.

original_title: Energy Transfer-Mediated Carboamination of Alkenes to Access γ-Amino-1,3-dicarbonyl Scaffolds
title: A single bifunctional reagent turns alkenes into γ-amino-1,3-dicarbonyls
blurb: An energy-transfer, visible-light carboamination built around an enyl oxime ester reagent that generates its carbon radical through a resonance-driven spin center shift. The reagent itself is easy to make from cheap feedstock, and it works across a wide range of alkenes, which is the part that makes this more than just a clever radical trick.

original_title: Mechanochemical Activation of Strontium for the Selective Cross-Coupling of Chlorosilanes
title: Ball-milled strontium cracks selective Si-Si heterocoupling
blurb: Chlorosilane reductive coupling has been stuck making only homocoupled Si-Si bonds for decades, with selective heterocoupling needing stepwise silicon-nucleophile generation or electrochemistry. Mechanochemically activating strontium metal by ball milling gets the selective cross-coupling directly, the kind of unglamorous fix this field has needed for a while.

original_title: Sterling Expands ADC Manufacturing Capacity and Capabilities - CHEManager
title: Sterling adds more ADC manufacturing capacity
blurb: Straight capacity-expansion news for Sterling's ADC manufacturing, no numbers attached. More room for a drug class everyone's betting on, but that's all there is to it here.

original_title: Nitrogen-functionalized 2-deoxy sp2-iminoglycolipids: Stereoselective synthesis and biological evaluation
title: Dialing in the nitrogen on an anti-inflammatory glycolipid
blurb: Sp2-iminoglycolipids like the lead dodecylsulfonyl-nojirimycin compound get their immunomodulatory punch from the twelve-carbon sulfonyl tail. This one keeps that tail fixed and goes after the sugar-like glycone side instead, adding nitrogen groups to see if it sharpens the anti-inflammatory activity further. Incremental SAR, but that's how this family has actually gotten better over the years.

original_title: Structure-Based Design of Potent Pan-YTHDF Ligands
title: One ligand that hits all three YTHDF m6A readers at once
blurb: A structure-based campaign lands compound 34, a pan-YTHDF inhibitor that binds YTHDF1, 2, and 3 with comparable affinity (Kd 0.14 µM against YTHDF2) while leaving the YTHDC1 and YTHDC2 readers alone. Crystal structures across six family members back up where that selectivity comes from. Real binding numbers and real selectivity data, not just a hit.

original_title: 1,2-Alkylthiocyanation of 1,3-Enynes Enabled by Photoredox and Copper Catalysis
title: Turning enynes into propargyl thiocyanates in one pot
blurb: Propargyl thiocyanates are handy building blocks but a pain to make cleanly. Pairing photoredox with copper catalysis stitches together 1,3-enynes, NH4SCN, and NHPI esters directly into them, redox-neutral and with a broad substrate scope, with mechanistic work pointing to a SET/EDA pathway behind it. Multicomponent reaction as usual, but a genuinely useful shortcut to a fiddly target.

original_title: Cation-surface RADA16-based self-assembling peptide hydrogel with high adhesion and osteogenesis promoting bone regeneration.
title: A stickier self-assembling peptide gel for bone repair
blurb: RADA16 is a well-worn self-assembling peptide scaffold; this version adds a cationic surface tweak aimed at stronger tissue adhesion and reportedly promotes osteogenesis for bone regeneration. Short on specifics beyond that, but the adhesion angle is the new piece here.

original_title: Why would Chlorobenzene be less cancerous than benzene?
title: Why would Chlorobenzene be less cancerous than benzene?
blurb: Benzene is classified as a carcinogen while chlorobenzene is not. Why do you think this is? As far as I understand it can participate in the same CYP450 mediated oxidation to form a (chloro)benzene oxide. It makes sense to me why toluene would be less dangerous as other oxidation products (benzoic acid) can be formed but I dont see this as a possibility for chloro benzene. Are there other factors in play? Is it because its potentiel carcinogenicity has not been investigated? Would be happy to hear your thoughts (or the answer if you know)

original_title: 100 ns Molecular Dynamics Simulation of Ozempic (Semaglutide) Bound to the GLP-1 Receptor
title: 100 ns Molecular Dynamics Simulation of Ozempic (Semaglutide) Bound to the GLP-1 Receptor
blurb: Here’s a molecular dynamics simulation I ran of semaglutide, the active ingredient in Ozempic, bound to the GLP-1 receptor. This is a 100-nanosecond molecular dynamics simulation showing how the peptide and receptor move and interact over time. Unlike a static crystal structure, MD allows us to observe protein flexibility, ligand motion, and changes in the binding environment. GLP-1 receptor activation plays an important role in insulin secretion, appetite regulation, and blood glucose control, making it a major therapeutic target for type 2 diabetes and obesity.
